name: Optical Dynamic Range Veil (Sensor Clash)
description: A brutal caliper engineered to unmask forged AI skies and impossibly perfect black-hole splices. Every real-world physical camera sensor is strictly handicapped by a finite 'Dynamic Range'—overexposure violently 'clips' into pure white data voids, while underexposure inevitably bleeds with chaotic electronic sensor noise. Generative AI and sloppy Photoshoppers routinely defy this bedrock physics, spawning hybrid nightmares: shadows as impossibly clean as the cosmic void, or blazing suns that absurdly retain ultra-smooth, perfectly preserved micro-details. This radar hunts that exact insolence.
algorithm: Highlight Edge Clipping & Deep-Shadow Noise Floor Contradiction
mechanism: It dissects the explosive exposure Histogram curve, staring directly off the two extreme cliffs: Pure White (Highlights) and Pure Black (Shadows). In authentic glass optics, blown-out highlights result in the RGB channels being violently and linearly sheared off at exactly 255. AI or composite elements 'forget' this, rendering bright areas with computationally smooth, physically absurd gradients. Conversely, genuine shadows must scream with the background radiation of sensor noise. AI hallucinates absolute darkness as flawless, sterile '0,0,0' black—a brutal inorganic signature completely betraying physical reality.
parameters: Core Engine: Linear Histogram Differential, Scanners: RGB Hard-Clipping Analyzer & Shadow Sensor Noise Floor Modeler
accuracy: Solid (67-78%) - Lightning fast and devastatingly effective at executing cases involving sloppy HDR compositing or impossibly lit fake panoramas.
source: Environmental Digital Illuminant & Finite Sensor Range Forensics
useCase: Strictly monitors extreme lighting topographies. Instantly triggers the executioner's alarm if a dimwit cuts a person out of a blown-out, sun-drenched beach photo and dumps them into a moody dark alley without computationally synchronizing the Dynamic Range boundaries.

references.title: Kee, E., & Farid, H. (2010). Exposing digital forgeries from 3-D lighting environments. IEEE TIFS.
Gonzalez, R.C. & Woods, R.E. (2018). Digital Image Processing. 4th Edition. Pearson.
Lukas, J. et al. (2006). Digital Camera Identification from Sensor Pattern Noise. IEEE TIFS.

strengths:
• Entirely ignores deepfake facial geometry and plunges directly into the foundational lighting laws of physics. Highly lethal against lazy editors who crank the Curves/Levels sliders without mathematically synchronizing the background ISO grain.
• Instantly execution-style condemns Midjourney’s impossibly perfect sunset skies that magically lack any true structural optical highlight clipping.
limitations:
• The forensic judgment turns chaotic (rampant False Positives) if tracking multi-thousand-dollar Cinema rigs (e.g., ARRI/RED RAW) boasting massive 15-stop Dynamic Ranges, producing natively clean shadows and ultra-smooth soft-clipped highlights.
• Can be entirely disarmed if a hyper-aware elite VFX artist intentionally injects precisely calculated matched 'Film Grain' into the forged shadows to perfectly spoof the noise-floor radar.
